rules: The complete elaborated target contract is fixed; boundary selection must not strengthen its assumptions or weaken its conclusion.
Select expanded mathematical nodes from actual source applications and declaration dependencies, not the import graph.
Mathlib proof bodies normally stop at the background boundary; retain definitions and instantiated interfaces. Library location alone does not justify granting the target or an equivalent answer.
A project theorem may be granted as a named background tool with its full interface and a mathematical stopping reason. Do not hide the substantive target argument in a background lemma.
Group definitions, instances and routine implementation lemmas as context only with an explicit reason. Context grouping never deletes their dependencies from the coverage check.
The conceptual-depth limit is advisory, not permission to omit a dependency or silently grant a theorem. Record an explicit boundary or an unresolved scope issue.
Use one consistent boundary for a correct reference and all mutations derived from it. Freeze the plan before detailed drafting; revisions require a new recorded plan checkpoint.
The reviewer judges the mathematical suitability of the boundary independently; graph closure and Lean compilation do not certify the English proof.
